It has been said that there is an omission in the speech, and the meaning is: "Have you seen the one who denies the Recompense, whether he is right or wrong?"

Muqatil and al-Kalbi said: it was revealed concerning al-'As ibn Wa'il al-Sahmi.

Al-Suddi said: concerning al-Walid ibn al-Mughirah.

Al-Dahhak said: concerning 'Amr ibn 'A'idh.

Ibn Jurayj said: concerning Abu Sufyan. It has also been said: concerning a man among the hypocrites.

The majority of readers read *a-ra'ayta* with the second hamzah retained.

al-Kisa'i read it with the second hamzah dropped.

al-Zajjaj said: one does not say *ryta* for *ra'ayta*; rather, the alif of interrogation made the hamzah into an alif.

It is also permissible that it be a conjunction (*'atf*) upon "the one who denies," either as conjunction of a substance upon a substance, or of a description upon a description.

On the second view, it is in the position of the accusative, being conjoined to the relative clause, which is itself in the position of the accusative.

The meaning of *sahun* (heedless) is: negligent, not caring about it. al-Nakha'i said: ﴿Who are heedless of their prayer﴾ is the one who, when he prostrates, says with his head like this and like this, turning aside.

Qutrub said: it is the one who neither recites nor remembers Allah.

Ibn Mas'ud recited: "Those who are unmindful (*lahun*) of their prayer."

﴿And withhold the small kindnesses (*ma'un*).﴾

Ibn Abi Hatim and Ibn Mardawayh narrated from Qurrah ibn Da'mus al-Numayri that "they came as a delegation to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and said: 'O Messenger of Allah, what do you enjoin upon us?' He said: 'Do not withhold the *ma'un*.' They said: 'And what is the *ma'un*?' He said: 'In the stone, the iron, and in the water.' They said: 'Which iron?' He said: 'Your copper cooking pots, and the iron of the axe with which you work.' They said: 'And what is the stone?' He said: 'Your stone cooking pots.'"

Ibn Kathir said: "Extremely strange, and its ascription (to the Prophet) is objectionable, and its chain contains someone who is unknown."

Ibn Abi Shaybah and Ibn Jarir narrated from Sa'id ibn 'Iyad, from the Companions of the Prophet (ﷺ): "*al-Ma'un*: the axe, the pot, and the bucket."

Sa'id ibn Mansur, Ibn Abi Shaybah, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, al-Tabarani, al-Hakim, who declared it sound, al-Bayhaqi, and al-Diya' in *al-Mukhtarah* narrated through several chains from Ibn 'Abbas concerning the verse, that he said: "It is the lending of household goods."

al-Firyabi, Sa'id ibn Mansur, Ibn Abi Shaybah, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, al-Hakim, and al-Bayhaqi in his *Sunan* narrated from 'Ali ibn Abi Talib, who said: "*al-Ma'un* is the obligatory zakah. They show off with their prayer, ﴿and withhold﴾ their zakah."
